name: Small modular nuclear reactors
title: Small modular reactors: NRC Part 53 is final, power is not
question: Is small modular nuclear power viable now that the NRC's new licensing rule is final?
answer: The NRC's technology-inclusive licensing rule, Part 53, was published on 30 March 2026 and took effect on 29 April 2026: the regulatory precondition has crossed. NuScale's first planned plant, the UAMPS Carbon Free Power Project, was cancelled in 2023 on cost. Commercial power from a new small reactor in the US is the trigger still pending.
verdict_reason: Licensing has crossed; first-of-a-kind cost and commercial operation have not.

constraint.name: Licensing path and first-of-a-kind cost
constraint.detail: Advanced reactors needed a licensing framework built for them, then a first plant that delivers power at a price utilities accept.

crossing.text: 10 CFR part 53 takes effect (licensing crossed); commercial operation pending.

graveyard.name: UAMPS Carbon Free Power Project (NuScale)
graveyard.how: Cancelled, November 2023, after cost estimates rose

evidence.text: NRC final rule: Risk-Informed, Technology-Inclusive Regulatory Framework for Advanced Reactors (part 53), effective 29 April 2026.
